fact_check_log.claim: As at November 2026, the form of the ceremony sits in section 45 of the Marriage Act 1961, and the celebrant's explanation sits in section 46.
Takeaway 2: s45(2) words, or words to that effect, in front of the celebrant and witnesses (non-minister celebrant).
It is sufficient for each of you to say ... the words set out in section 45(2) (quoted exactly).
s46(1) monitum said by a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination (quoted exactly, no commentary).
A minister of religion may use any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient by their religious body or organisation.
The law asks for these words 'or words to that effect'.
In New Zealand, couples can write their own vows as long as each says words to the effect of 'I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner'.
FAQ: The Marriage Act 1961 asks each of you to say the section 45(2) words 'or words to that effect'.
FAQ: shortest vows are the s45(2) words, or words to that effect, before celebrant and witnesses.
If you marry legally overseas, the legal wording follows that country (takeaway 4 and Marrying overseas).
Keep vows to 1 to 2 minutes each (stated as our advice, not attributed).
Every example runs well under a minute (longest example about 70 words).
Many couples add a few lines of their own. (generalisation; edit replaces it)
Short wedding vows ... land harder than most long ones. (comparative; edit replaces it)

One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact. (brand-facts.md Claims we can make: one Wedded Advisor single point of contact; plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world)
Wedded Concierge can carry the logistics while you work on the words. (not a Confirmed claim; edit replaces it)
